# Notespice

> A self-hosted notes application with no database. Every note is a plain
> markdown file on the operator's own disk. Published by Lightmorphic Ltd
> under the MIT licence.

Notespice is a notes app you run yourself, usually as a single Docker
container. It stores each note as an ordinary `.md` file in a folder you
choose, so the notes can be read, moved, backed up or edited with any other
tool, and nothing has to be exported to leave. There is no database, no
account system and no third-party server involved.

The editor supports the parts of GitHub Flavored Markdown people use most:
tables, footnotes, task lists, strikethrough and GitHub-style callouts. It
writes those back out as ordinary markdown. It is not a complete CommonMark
or GFM implementation; constructs such as reference links, setext headings,
indented code blocks and raw HTML blocks are not supported.

It can be installed to a phone or desktop like an app, follows the system
light or dark setting, and exports every note and attachment to a dated zip
that imports straight back in.

## Pages
- [Home](https://notespice.org/): what it is, a live editor to try, and how to run it
- [Privacy](https://notespice.org/privacy.html): the site collects nothing; the host keeps ordinary server logs
- [Cookies](https://notespice.org/cookies.html): none are set
- [Terms](https://notespice.org/terms.html): MIT licence, no warranty, England and Wales
- [Accessibility](https://notespice.org/accessibility.html): what was tested and what was not
- [Complaints](https://notespice.org/complaints.html): how to raise a problem
